# Paper tables (generated by paper_tables.py, no new runs)

## T1. Re-layout x request moves (development seeds 1-3, 18 paired cases, B* annealing off in every cell)

Configuration used for this grid: affinity placement, request moves capped at 300 per round (the configuration at the time of the experiment, not FROZEN-1). Raw P99 completion latency in seconds.

| Cell | Re-layout | Request moves | Mean P99 (s) | Median (s) | Geometric mean (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B* (reference) | annealing swaps | inside annealing | 579 | 540 | 507 |
| A | no | no | 3948 | 3736 | 3725 |
| B | no | yes | 1957 | 1938 | 1741 |
| C | yes | no | 639 | 588 | 562 |
| D | yes | yes | 166 | 135 | 150 |

Conditional effects, as factors by which the geometric-mean P99 shrinks (95% bootstrap interval over cases):

| Effect | Factor | Interval |
|---|---|---|
| moves, on a fixed layout (A to B) | x2.1 | x1.8 to x2.5 |
| moves, with re-layout (C to D) | x3.7 | x3.2 to x4.4 |
| re-layout, without moves (A to C) | x6.6 | x5.1 to x8.6 |
| re-layout, with moves (B to D) | x11.6 | x9.0 to x14.8 |
| both together (A to D) | x24.8 | x20.5 to x29.5 |

Interaction (log scale, 0 = the effects multiply independently): -0.56 (-0.81 to -0.31). Moves help more when the layout adapts: x3.7 with re-layout against x2.1 without. Consistency check: A to D = (A to B)(B to D) = (A to C)(C to D).

## T2. Absolute P99 completion latency on held-out seeds 4-10 (FROZEN-1 at 60 s vs the existing methods)

| Family | Load | Cases | FROZEN-1 (s) | B* (s) | RL (s) | Calibrated RL (s) | Requests per P99 (mean) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Azure | 50% | 7 | 120 | 235 | 158 | 286 | 10566 |
| Azure | 70% | 7 | 143 | 450 | 670 | 621 | 14699 |
| Azure | 85% | 7 | 182 | 632 | 1018 | 895 | 17899 |
| Huawei | 50% | 7 | 119 | 385 | 133 | 251 | 14946 |
| Huawei | 70% | 7 | 147 | 670 | 511 | 518 | 20968 |
| Huawei | 85% | 7 | 188 | 925 | 827 | 806 | 25457 |

The P99 of one run rests on about 1% of the requests counted in the last column (e.g. 200 requests for 20,000). At 50% load even a system with no queueing and no cold starts has a P99 near 88 s (exponential task durations, Monte Carlo floor), so relative gains are compressed there; 85% load is where the controllers differ most.

## T3. Admission control on the overload set ({B*, ours} x {off, on}) (20 cases: Azure and Huawei overload windows, seeds 1-10)

Admission rule (both controllers, untuned): admit a request only if the requests in the system are at most 1.0 x the number of container slots. Goodput = workflows finishing within 3 x their unloaded critical path, per second. The controller in these runs is ours in its k-median version of the time, not FROZEN-1; the admission effect is the comparison of interest.

| Controller | No admission: goodput | With admission: goodput | Rejected | P99 of admitted (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B* | 2.32 | 7.67 | 59% | 1370 -> 224 |
| Ours | 10.30 | 23.29 | 32% | 703 -> 130 |

Admission multiplies goodput by x3.3 for B* and x2.3 for our controller; with and without admission our controller is ahead (x4.4 without, x3.0 with). Cases: 20.
